details.description: Qwen2.5-Coder-32B is the 32.5-billion-parameter base checkpoint and flagship size in Alibaba's Qwen2.5-Coder family, open-sourced by the Qwen team on November 12, 2024. It was pretrained on 5.5 trillion tokens of source code, text-code grounding data, and synthetic data. As a base (non-instruct) model, Qwen states it is not meant for direct conversational use and instead serves as a foundation for fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, or continued pretraining.
advantages: Pretrained on 5.5 trillion tokens of source code, text-code grounding data, and synthetic data, per Qwen's model card.
Natively supports a 32,768-token context window, extendable to 131,072 tokens via YaRN scaling, per Qwen's model card.
Released under the Apache 2.0 license, permitting commercial use and redistribution.
disadvantages: Is a base model, not tuned for instructions; Qwen states it does not recommend using base language models for conversations and instead recommends fine-tuning, RLHF, or continued pretraining.
Text-only input and output, with no vision or audio support.
use_cases: Fine-tuning into custom coding assistants, agents, or domain-specific code models.
Continued pretraining or RLHF starting point for organizations building their own code LLMs.
Code completion and generation research or benchmarking as an open-weight foundation model.

notes: Base (non-instruct) checkpoint. The published Aider/McEval/MdEval scores refer to the Instruct variant, not this base model, so those are correctly excluded. However, the maker's Qwen2.5-Coder Technical Report (arXiv 2409.12186) does publish base-model-specific scores (HumanEval, HumanEval+, MBPP, MBPP+, BigCodeBench-Complete) in its base-model evaluation section, which were added since they were missing from the family blog post the researcher checked.
